clips.title: The story
paras: Assigned by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village, this task sends young Horde adventurers to curb the destructive poaching of the local Palemane gnolls. By culling their tanners, skinners, and poachers, you protect Mulgore's wildlife and learn the tauren philosophy of living in balance with the Earth Mother.

The tauren hold deep reverence for the natural world, taking from it only what is necessary to survive and honoring the Earth Mother in all things. The Palemane gnolls, having settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, harbor no such respect. Rather than hunting in moderation, they aggressively butcher wildlife across the plains, leaving stripped carcasses and upset ecosystems in their wake. For a people striving to build a peaceful homeland in Mulgore, this reckless slaughter cannot be tolerated.

Baine Bloodhoof initially hoped to resolve the matter peacefully, attempting to open dialogue with the encroaching gnolls. The Palemanes rejected every overture, answering diplomacy with hostility and continued devastation. Seeing that negotiation is futile, Baine turns to force. Young braves are sent directly to their hunting camps to put down the poachers, tanners, and skinners before the grasslands suffer permanent damage.

This mission serves as a rite of passage and a moral lesson for growing champions. Upon returning from the culling, Baine reminds the adventurer that taking life must never be done out of malice, but out of necessity to maintain harmony. Life and death exist as an interconnected circle where one cannot thrive without the other, a foundational truth every guardian of Mulgore must carry forward.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Friend, there are many conflicts that wound this land. It is my hope that you will not bear witness to as many of them as I have. Yet there is one that I would ask you to seek out. It will give you some sense of how terrible, if left unchecked, even a small threat can be to the land.
Palemane gnolls have settled to the south of Bloodhoof and in a cave to the west. They disrespect our attempts to communicate with them, and they slay the wildlife of Mulgore unbridled.
Words are no longer the answer.

clips.title: Progress
paras: If the Palemanes had respected the land and its inhabitants more, this conflict would have never occurred.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Friend, it is good you've taken my task seriously. Respect of the land and its creatures is important. Death and life are a circle... A necessity. One cannot exist without the other. Take time to ponder this and do well to never forget it.
